sebra_swart_wit.af: Die sebra is swart en wit.
sebra_swart_wit.en: The zebra is black and white.

i_ek_soek_melk.af: Ja, ek soek melk en brood.
i_ek_soek_melk.en: Yes, I'm looking for milk and bread.

i_kaart_betaal.af: Kan ek met my kaart betaal?

i_wil_graag_koffie.af: Ek wil graag 'n koffie hê, asseblief.

i_rekening.af: Kan ons die rekening kry, asseblief?
i_rekening.en: Can we have the bill, please?

i_nog_wors.en: Would you like some more sausage?

i_skottelgoed.af: Kan ek met die skottelgoed help?
i_skottelgoed.en: Can I help with the dishes?

i_sondag_kuier.en: We're coming to visit on Sunday.

i_met_pieter.af: Kan ek met Pieter praat, asseblief?
i_met_pieter.en: May I speak to Pieter, please?

i_nie_hier_nie.af: Hy is nie nou hier nie.

i_kan_nie_hoor.af: Jammer, ek kan jou nie hoor nie.

i_ek_eet_nou.en: We're eating now. Come and sit!

i_ons_gebraai.en: We had a braai last night.

i_hulle_see_toe.af: Hulle gaan volgende week see toe.
i_hulle_see_toe.en: They're going to the seaside next week.

i_boek_gelees.af: Ek het die boek klaar gelees.

i_wat_gedoen.af: Wat het jy die naweek gedoen?
i_wat_gedoen.en: What did you do on the weekend?

i_het_gewerk.af: Ek het die hele dag gewerk.

i_gou_winkel.en: I'm just popping to the shops.

i_weet_dat_moeg.af: Ek weet dat hy moeg is.

i_nooit_gewoon.af: Ek het nooit daar gewoon nie.

i_want_moeg.af: Ek bly tuis, want ek is moeg.
i_want_moeg.en: I'm staying home, because I'm tired.

i_omdat_moeg.af: Ek bly tuis omdat ek moeg is.
i_omdat_moeg.en: I'm staying home because I'm tired.

i_as_dit_reen.af: As dit reën, bly ons binne.
i_as_dit_reen.en: If it rains, we stay inside.

i_toe_ek_klein.af: Toe ek klein was, het ons op 'n plaas gebly.
i_toe_ek_klein.en: When I was small, we lived on a farm.

i_nou_nou.en: I'll be there in a little while.

i_boer_plan.en: Where there's a will, there's a way.

i_bal_mis.af: Hy het die bal mis geslaan.

i_kat_uit_sak.af: Die aap is uit die mou.
i_kat_uit_sak.en: The cat's out of the bag.

i_sommer.af: Ek bel sommer net om te hoor hoe dit gaan.
i_sommer.en: I'm just calling to see how you are.

i_bakkie.en: Chuck it on the back of the bakkie.

i_verskoon_my.af: Verskoon my, waar is die stasie?
i_verskoon_my.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

i_draai_links.en: Turn left at the traffic light.

i_vyf_minute.af: Dis net vyf minute se stap.

i_kaartjie.en: One ticket to Cape Town, please.

i_klim_af.af: Ek klim by die volgende halte af.
i_klim_af.en: I'm getting off at the next stop.

i_lughawe.af: Kan jy my by die lughawe kom haal?
i_lughawe.en: Can you pick me up at the airport?

i_hoes.en: I've been coughing for three days.

i_afspraak.en: I'd like to make an appointment.

i_rus.af: Jy moet rus en baie water drink.
i_rus.en: You must rest and drink lots of water.

i_wat_werk_jy.en: What do you do for a living?

i_hoe_lank_hier.af: Hoe lank bly jy al hier?
i_hoe_lank_hier.en: How long have you lived here?

i_vrye_tyd.af: Wat doen jy in jou vrye tyd?
i_vrye_tyd.en: What do you do in your free time?

i_hou_van_stap.af: Ek hou van stap en lees.

i_pragtige_dag.en: It's a beautiful day, isn't it?

i_gaan_reen.en: It's going to rain this afternoon.

levels.blurb: Greetings, family, animals, food, colours and numbers.
Real conversations, verbs and tenses, word order, and the slang people actually use.

notes.i_sak_nodig: Shop staff often use "jy"; to an older customer they'd say "Het u ...?"
notes.i_wil_graag_koffie: Note "hê" (to have) at the end with "wil graag".
notes.i_kom_in: "Kom binne" is the everyday way to welcome someone in.
notes.i_koue_drankie: A "koeldrank" is a soft drink, like a South African "cold drink".
notes.i_moet_ry: "Ry" = to drive off, to leave (by car).
notes.i_hoe_laat: "Julle" = you, when talking to more than one person.
notes.i_ek_eet_nou: Present tense: one form for every person.
notes.i_gister_geeet: Past tense: het + ge- form. Note the trema: geëet.
notes.i_sal_more_eet: Future: sal + verb at the end.
notes.i_hulle_see_toe: "see toe" = to the sea; the direction word comes after.
notes.i_gou_winkel: "Gou" = quickly; it makes it sound casual.
notes.i_vandag_werk_toe: Verb second: the verb comes straight after "Vandag".
notes.i_weet_dat_moeg: After "dat" the verb goes to the end.
notes.i_want_moeg: After "want" the word order stays normal.
notes.i_omdat_moeg: After "omdat" the verb goes to the end.
notes.i_as_dit_reen: After an "as ..." part, the verb comes first: "bly ons".
notes.i_toe_ek_klein: "Toe" = when, for the past. The verb goes to the end: "klein was".
notes.i_praat_kaf: Informal. Fine with friends, a bit rude to someone's face.
notes.i_nou_nou: Informal. "Nou-nou" = in a while, not right now.
notes.i_boer_plan: Idiom: literally "a farmer makes a plan".
notes.i_kat_uit_sak: Idiom: literally "the monkey is out of the sleeve". The secret is out.
notes.i_draai_links: In South Africa a traffic light is a "robot".
notes.i_watter_bus: In South Africa a "taxi" is usually a minibus taxi. "Stad toe" = to town; the direction word comes after.
notes.i_lughawe: "Kom haal" = come and fetch, the usual way to say pick someone up.
notes.i_kop_seer: "Seer" = sore. "My kop is seer" = I have a headache.
notes.i_hoes: "Al" with the present tense = have been ... for.
notes.i_pille: In Afrikaans you "drink" pills and medicine.
